questions.text:
If '[latex] \rightarrow [/latex]' denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of the words [walk [latex] \rightarrow [/latex] jog [latex] \rightarrow [/latex] sprint] is analogous to [bothered [latex] \rightarrow [/latex] ________ [latex] \rightarrow [/latex] daunted].
Which one of the given options is appropriate to fill the blank?
questions.solution:
walk [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] jog [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] sprint: increasing speed.
bothered [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] ___ [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] daunted: increasing level of being disturbed / discouraged. Fazed (disturbed, unsettled) fits between them.

phased (done in stages), phrased (worded), fused (joined) have unrelated meanings.

Answer: fazed

questions.text:
Two wizards try to create a spell using all the four elements, water, air, fire, and earth. For this, they decide to mix all these elements in all possible orders. They also decide to work independently. After trying all possible combination of elements, they conclude that the spell does not work.
How many attempts does each wizard make before coming to this conclusion, independently?
questions.solution:
Each attempt is one order of the 4 different elements: [latex]4!=24[/latex] orders.

The wizards work independently, so each of them tries all 24.

Answer: 24

questions.text:
In an engineering college of 10,000 students, 1,500 like neither their core branches nor other branches. The number of students who like their core branches is 1/4th of the number of students who like other branches. The number of students who like both their core and other branches is 500.
The number of students who like their core branches is
questions.solution:
Students liking at least one [latex]=10000-1500=8500[/latex].
Let core = C, other = O with [latex]C=O/4[/latex], i.e. [latex]O=4C[/latex].

[latex]C+O-\text{both}=8500\Rightarrow C+4C-500=8500\Rightarrow C=1800[/latex]

Answer: 1,800

questions.text:
For positive non-zero real variables [latex]x [/latex] and [latex]y [/latex], if

[latex] \ln \left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right)=\frac{1}{2}[\ln (x)+\ln (y)] [/latex]

then, the value of [latex]\frac{x}{y}+\frac{y}{x} [/latex] is
questions.solution:
[latex]\ln\frac{x+y}{2}=\ln\sqrt{xy}\Rightarrow\frac{x+y}{2}=\sqrt{xy}[/latex]

AM = GM holds only when [latex]x=y[/latex] (equivalently [latex](\sqrt x-\sqrt y)^2=0[/latex]).

[latex]\frac xy+\frac yx=1+1=2[/latex]

Answer: 2

questions.text: In the sequence 6, 9, 14, x, 30, 41, a possible value of x is
questions.solution:
Differences: 9[latex]-[/latex]6 = 3, 14[latex]-[/latex]9 = 5, then 7, 9, 11 (odd numbers).

[latex]x=14+7=21[/latex]; check [latex]21+9=30[/latex], [latex]30+11=41[/latex] True

Answer: 21
